title: Pauli-ball discrepancy and stability of quantum codes
abstract: The Pauli-ball discrepancy, a quadratic discrepancy summed over all error radii, measures how uniformly the Pauli error images of a $K$-dimensional quantum code cover the $d$-dimensional Hilbert space. At parameters attaining equality in the quantum Singleton bound with minimum code distance $\geq3$, or in the one-error Hamming bound with prime-power local dimension, the discrepancy of every projector of the prescribed rank equals an explicit benchmark plus an exact nonnegative remainder, which vanishes precisely for pure quantum maximum-distance-separable codes and nondegenerate perfect codes, respectively. For a Pauli ball of radius $e$ below half the target distance and size $V_e$, this remainder linearly bounds the squared Hilbert--Schmidt distance of the error-image Gram matrix from the identity. When $KV_e\leq d$, it linearly bounds the diamond error and entanglement infidelity of a noise-independent polar recovery under any noise in that ball's span. For five qubits, we obtain the sharp rank-two Gram constant and exact logical channels of rotated codes attaining this linear order in diamond error. For pure states, the discrepancy equals a pure-state benchmark plus a positive weighted sum of marginal-purity defects, so absolutely maximally entangled states, when they exist, are exactly the minimizers.
summary: This theoretical paper develops the Pauli-ball discrepancy as a quantitative measure of how well a quantum code covers its error space. It establishes deep mathematical links showing that minimizing this discrepancy is equivalent to achieving optimal error correction properties, particularly for highly entangled states. This work provides advanced diagnostic tools for assessing quantum code performance.
main_problem: The paper quantifies the uniform coverage of the physical Hilbert space by Pauli error images of a quantum code using the Pauli-ball discrepancy, linking this measure to the code's error correction stability.
main_result: The discrepancy excess provides explicit linear bounds on the squared Gram defect, and the minimum discrepancy is achieved exactly by highly entangled states like absolutely maximally entangled states.
method: The analysis employs spectral methods, relating the discrepancy to quantum enumerators and solving the problem via Delsarte linear programming techniques.
model_or_system: The system is a quantum error correcting code defined by a rank-$K$ projector $P$ acting on a Hilbert space $H = (\mathbb{C}^q)^{\otimes n}$. Errors are modeled by Pauli operators within a specified error ball.
key_observables: Pauli-ball discrepancy ($D_Q(P)$), discrepancy excess ($g(P)$), squared Gram defect ($\|G_e - I_K V_e\|^2_{	ext{HS}}$), diamond error, and entanglement infidelity.
important_parameters: Quantum MDS parameters, one-error Hamming parameters, and the error radius $e$ relative to the code distance $\Delta$.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on specific parameter regimes (MDS/Hamming) and the assumption that the error model is restricted to the span of the Pauli ball.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from defining the Pauli-ball discrepancy and its relation to code coverage, deriving spectral identities using quantum enumerators, establishing linear bounds between discrepancy and Gram defect, and finally applying these results to specific cases like pure states and five-qubit systems.
why_interesting: The rigorous mathematical connection established between a global geometric measure (discrepancy) and local error metrics (Gram matrix deviation, fidelity) provides powerful diagnostic tools for characterizing the performance limits of quantum codes.
